name: WAPLES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Auditor has implied statutory authorization to sue the Attorney General for mandamus to enforce the statutory duty to provide legal advice, but the Attorney General's advice, even if not a direct answer, fulfilled her obligation, and the Auditor's powers are defined by the Legislature, not inherent constitutional authority.

name: Waples, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the majority opinion affirming the trial court's decision that the search was lawful and speedy-trial rights were not violated.

name: CARROLL, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while individuals have a legitimate privacy interest in real-time CSLI, the warrantless ping in this case was justified by exigent circumstances.

name: Reiber, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that defendants do not have a vested right in an expired limitations period, and the retroactive application of the statute of limitations does not violate the Vermont Constitution.

name: Eaton, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Education Clause does not require the state to provide school choice at its expense, and the parents failed to demonstrate that the current statutory scheme results in substantial inequality of educational opportunities or violates the Common Benefits Clause.

name: CARROLL, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while individuals have a legitimate privacy interest in real-time cell site location information requiring a warrant, exigent circumstances justified the warrantless ping in this specific murder case.

name: EATON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Chapter II, § 42 of the Vermont Constitution does not apply to municipal elections, thus the statute allowing noncitizens to vote in Montpelier local elections is constitutional.

name: CARROLL, J.
description: Concurred, argued that plaintiffs failed to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the education funding and property taxation system caused the alleged unequal educational opportunities or disproportionate taxation.

name: ROBINSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court applied an incorrect legal standard for the suppression question, and the trooper's active visual search for the bullet exceeded his limited license to be on the property, violating defendant's constitutional rights.

name: EATON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ammunition cartridge was seen in plain view by the officer from a legally permitted location, and the trial court did not err in admitting the defendant's racial-animus-related language.

name: Cohen, J.
description: Concurred, argued that evidence seized by federal Border Patrol agents during roving patrols on interior roads, in violation of Article 11 of the Vermont Constitution, is inadmissible in state criminal proceedings to protect individual liberty and judicial integrity.

name: Carroll, J.
description: Dissented, argued that evidence lawfully obtained by federal Border Patrol agents exercising exclusive authority to safeguard the U.S. border should be admissible in Vermont criminal court proceedings, consistent with controlling precedents and the purposes of the exclusionary rule.
